result.title: Beyond Accuracy: Information-Theoretic Decoder Evaluation Under Latent Intent
result.summary: A central challenge in assistive brain-to-robot control is decoding a user's latent intent from complex and noisy brain signals. Prior approaches evaluate decoders as single-trial classifiers with accuracy-based metrics, but this neglects the inherently sequential nature of assistive control. Since a planner must integrate intermittent, noisy decoder outputs over time, single-step accuracy can only be a proxy when predicting downstream task performance. We formalize brain-to-robot control as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and prove that there is a sharp phase transition: regret is uniformly bounded across the horizon as long as pairs of goals are all decoder-distinguishable, but grows linearly otherwise. We show that a single channel statistic, the worst-pair Chernoff information $Γ_{\min}$ sets this boundary. Then, we derive a closed-form regret predictor $U_{\mathrm{id}}(C)$, that can be computed from any confusion matrix in $O(K^2)$ time. Across two domains spanning orthogonal information channels, we show that $U_{\mathrm{id}}$ predicts cumulative planning regret beyond what accuracy can explain. We then highlight a pathological accuracy trap, in which two decoders have identical validation accuracy 35.1% on real EEG data (BNCI2014001 subject 5) but result in a difference of $9.6\times$ in held-out regret, which $U_{\mathrm{id}}$ predicts. Same-signal control confirms $U_{\mathrm{id}}$'s advantage with decoders that span independent feature channels. Ultimately, our work provides a drop-in diagnostic to evaluate and select sensors and decoders in sequential assistive control.

AI.brief_summary: 将脑机到机器人的辅助控制形式化为 POMDP，证明以最差目标对 Chernoff 信息 Γ_min 为边界存在遗憾的相变，并给出可由混淆矩阵在 O(K²) 内算出的闭式遗憾预测器 U_id；在真实 EEG 上展示同准确率 35.1% 的两解码器留出遗憾相差 9.6 倍。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「潜在意图可区分性决定下游序列决策表现、单步准确率只是代理」的论证与信息论诊断，可能为 LVR 中判断潜在视觉证据是否足以支撑多步推理与停止决策提供可核查的评价思路，但领域较远，迁移需验证。
